match.reason: None of the bank points teaches human resource management as the way a business finds, trains, rewards and looks after its staff; the closest, 'Business resources', only covers labour as an input, and the others cover collaboration, starting resources or HR measurement at a different depth.

note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Remember, other: The remember line says HRM 'looks after the people', but the card uses 'looking after' as only one of four parts (finding, training, rewarding, looking after). This could lead students to treat HRM as just looking after staff, which matters in question b where they must tell the parts apart. Wording such as 'HRM is how a business manages its people' would avoid the clash.

rejected.title: Human resource management
card: Human resource management (HRM) is how a business manages its staff. It covers finding, training, rewarding and looking after them.
Finding staff means recruiting and choosing people with the right skills. Training helps them do their jobs well. Rewarding means pay and other benefits.
Looking after staff includes safe workplaces, fair treatment and support for their wellbeing. Staff who feel looked after are more likely to stay.
The aim of HRM is for staff to work well, so the business can compete better against other businesses.
rejected.remember: HRM looks after the people in a business so they work well and the business competes better.

a.q: Which of these is an example of human resource management?
opts: A manager runs a program to train new staff
A manager changes the prices of the products
A manager buys a new delivery van
A manager designs a new shop logo
a.why: Training staff is part of managing people, which is what HRM covers. The other options are about pricing, equipment and branding, which do not manage staff.
a.clue: Which one is about the people who work there?

b.q: Ravi owns a bakery in Ballarat. Staff keep leaving after a few months, so he raises their pay and starts regular chats about how they are coping. Which parts of HRM is he using?
opts: Rewarding staff and looking after them
Finding staff and training them
Finding staff and rewarding them
Training staff and looking after them
b.why: Higher pay is a reward, and chats about how staff are coping support their wellbeing, which is looking after them. Ravi is not hiring anyone new or teaching new skills, so finding and training are not part of these changes.
b.clue: Match each change to one part of HRM on the card.

b.q: Ravi owns a bakery in Ballarat. Staff keep leaving after a few months. He starts offering safe rosters, fair pay and regular check-ins. Why is this HRM?
opts: It looks after and rewards staff so they work well and stay
It lowers the price of the bread for customers
It adds a new product to the bakery menu
It cuts the cost of flour and other ingredients
b.why: Rosters, pay and check-ins are ways of rewarding and looking after staff, so they are HRM. The other options are about prices, products and costs of materials, not about managing people.
b.clue: Look at who the changes are for.

a.best: A manager runs a program to train new staff

b.best: It looks after and rewards staff so they work well and stay
